name: Redlining a contract without leaving Word
object: ChatGPT for Microsoft Word, a side panel inside Word that formats, revises and flags risk in a document in place, with Skills like Contract Review
audience: office workers and legal/ops teams who draft and redline documents in Word all day
message: This video tells Word users that ChatGPT now sits in the same window as the document, so formatting, redlining and risk review happen without switching apps.

moments.what: a plain title card reads the announcement
a ChatGPT side panel sits next to a Client Services Agreement in Word; the user attaches a template and asks ChatGPT to format the agreement to match it, and the document reflows with tracked changes
moments.copy: Format this agreement to match the attached template.

moments.what: the user attaches negotiation notes and asks ChatGPT to revise payment terms, then runs a Contract Review Skill that flags unresolved risks and decisions before the document is shared, with tracked changes and a summary of the dollar terms appearing in the chat
moments.copy: Use the Contract Review Skill to flag unresolved risks and decisions before I share this.

moments.what: kinetic type lists what ChatGPT can do in Word, formatting, planning, summarizing, editing, charting, redlining, work, then a closing card reads get started for free with the Word and Excel icons and the OpenAI mark
moments.copy: Use ChatGPT for formatting, planning, summarizing, editing, charting, redlining, work. Get started for free today.

cta: "Get started for free today", staged as a closing title card with the Word and Excel icons beside the OpenAI mark
why: Showing the tracked-change redline land directly inside the real document, not in a separate chat window, proves the pitch that this replaces app-switching rather than adding another tool to check.
